drafted_from: tool:check-texting-works-on-this-mac row in tools/send-messages/tool-rows.json, do-work/check-texting.mjs and test/check-texting.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Check that you can use Messages on my Mac, without sending anything." It runs tool:check-texting-works-on-this-mac once and says how many chats and which kinds of accounts Messages has.
no_lists_because: It names no list: it reads two counts from Messages when run, keeps nothing and sends nothing.
instructions: 1. Allow the app that runs the tool to control Messages in System Settings, Privacy & Security, Automation; without it the tool answers needs_access "automation" and reads nothing.
2. Your AI calls do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools with method tools:run, tool tool:check-texting-works-on-this-mac, input {computer: {"automate-an-app": {app: "com.apple.MobileSMS"}}}.
3. Read the answer: chats (how many), accounts (how many) and service_types (for example iMessage, SMS). No address, name or text is in it.
4. If it answers error cannot_read_messages_terms, the run could not read Messages' scripting terms; nothing was sent either way.

worked_examples.title: Messages ready, two kinds of account
worked_examples.ask: Can you use Messages on my Mac? Don't send anything.
worked_examples.given: From tools/send-messages/test/check-texting.test.mjs (osascript stood in for): Messages answers 12 chats and accounts of type iMessage, SMS and iMessage.
worked_examples.hands_back: chats 12, accounts 3, service_types ["SMS", "iMessage"], said "Messages on this Mac can be scripted: its terms compiled and it answered." With Automation not allowed it answers {needs_access: "automation", said: "Allow the app that runs this tool to control Messages in System Settings, Privacy & Security, Automation."}.
